note: One-time historical backfill covering 2026-08-04 13:00Z to 2026-08-05 13:00Z. Raw per-check telemetry captured from the live server before the persistent-volume migration, plus the events reconstructed from it. Listener counts during HTTP 404 outages were corrected to 0: the pre-fix code carried the last known count forward when a mount vanished, which concealed the audience loss. All other values are as recorded.

events.message: KPFT Main is DOWN — Source encoder disconnected (HTTP 404, Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8)

evidence: Icecast answered the request and returned HTTP 404 — the server process was alive and serving.
Mount /live_128 was not attached: no source client was connected to it.
A 404 on an Icecast mount means the SERVER is healthy and the SOURCE dropped — this is a studio-side fault, not a Pacifica server fault.
Only this stream was affected at this timestamp.
remediation: The Icecast server is healthy — this is a SOURCE-side failure.
Check the Barix encoder / studio streaming appliance is powered and online.
Verify the encoder’s network link and its Icecast source password.
The mount reappears automatically once the source reconnects.

events.message: KPFT Main failed a check — Connection reset by server (socket hang up)

evidence: The server accepted the connection then dropped it mid-transfer.
ALL 3 monitored streams failed at this same timestamp — a server-level or network-level event, not a per-stream fault.
Typical of an Icecast restart, a hit connection limit, or a proxy recycling connections.
remediation: Often transient: an Icecast restart, a connection-limit ceiling, or a proxy recycling.
If this repeats, check Icecast max-clients and server load.
